card.name: Garba
card.tagline: Gujarati devotional circle dance of Navaratri
card.profile: Garba is a ritualistic and devotional folk dance of Gujarat performed during the Hindu festival of Navaratri, dedicated to the worship of feminine energy (Shakti) (UNESCO). Dancers move counter-clockwise in a circle around a perforated earthenware pot lit with a lamp (garbo) or an image of the mother goddess Amba, using simple steps, singing and clapping that build from slow circular movements to fast whirling (UNESCO). The name derives from a Sanskrit word for womb, implying life and creation, and the dance fosters social and gender inclusivity across communities.
card.insight: Garba was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity on 6 December 2023 at the 18th session in Kasane, Botswana, becoming India's 15th element on the list (UNESCO/PIB).
